info.title: Quantustik Public API
info.description: Quantum-mechanics-based S&P 500 signal API. Free, open access.

get.description:
Realised outcome summary (win-rate + R-distribution) from stored events.

Registered before `/signals/{ticker}` so the literal `track-record` path
is not captured as a ticker. Pass `ticker` for a per-ticker record; omit
it for the portfolio-wide record. Small samples are flagged
`illustrative: true` and never presented as a reliable hit-rate — every
number is grounded in stored `tp_hit` / `stop_hit` / `position_closed`
events.

Quantum swing signal + forecast for one ticker.

Pass ``format=markdown`` (or ``Accept: text/markdown``) to get the same
data as a compact markdown signal card — renders natively in AI chat.

The JSON envelope carries a top-level ``disclaimer`` sentence, the same one
the list endpoint and the markdown card's footer carry.

All tickers from the latest scan, with optional server-side filters and cursor pagination.

**Backward-compatible**: no params returns same behavior as before (all results, no pagination).

**Filters** (all optional, combinable):
- min_conviction: only return tickers whose 3mo conviction score >= this value.
- verdict: only return tickers whose VERDICT (what the model thinks of the
  stock) matches — BUY / WAIT / EXIT, or the published labels
  BULLISH / NEUTRAL / BEARISH.
- timing: only return tickers whose ENTRY TIMING (should you buy right now)
  matches — BUY / WAIT / AVOID / WATCH.
- direction: deprecated alias for `timing`. It has always matched the entry
  facet, so it keeps doing exactly that: an existing integration returns the
  same rows it returns today. Re-pointing it at the verdict facet would have
  silently widened `direction=BUY` from "rows with a live, risk-gated entry"
  to "every bullish-leaning row" — a caller would get MORE rows, most with no
  entry price, and no way to notice.
- sector: partial, case-insensitive match against the ticker sector name.

**Pagination**: supply limit to activate cursor pagination; use next_cursor from the
response as the cursor param on the next request. Returns next_cursor=null when exhausted.

*Disclaimer: signals are for informational purposes only and do not constitute financial
advice. Always conduct independent research before making investment decisions.*

get.description:
Event history for a ticker: every signal opened, and how each one ended.

Depth does not vary by tier. Every feature map carries the same
``history_max_events``, and this route applies its own ceiling to everyone
via the ``limit`` query bound, so the clamp below can only ever return what
was asked for. It stays as the enforcement point rather than being deleted.

get.summary: Current market state — verdict, score, signal breakdown, action plan
get.description:
The market's current state: verdict, 0-100 score, the signal breakdown
behind it, how confident the model is, and the action plan that follows.

This is the whole market snapshot, not one number. `/market/indicators`
returns the same state as a row-per-signal sheet worded for a human.

get.summary: Deprecated alias of GET /api/v1/market — identical payload
get.description:
Deprecated alias of `GET /api/v1/market`, kept working permanently.

Returns exactly the same payload. Existing integrations do not need to
change; new ones should use `/api/v1/market`.

Every market indicator we compute, in plain English, with its live contribution.

The model weighs 18 signals into one score; this returns all 18 — not just the
handful the dashboard has room for — each with a plain-English label, its current
state, what that state means, which way it is pushing the verdict, and by how much.

Rows are grouped by what they are doing to the verdict (`groups`): pushing it
down, pushing it up, measured-but-silent, and no-data. `aggregate.arithmetic`
shows the sum that produces the score, so the verdict can be checked rather than
taken on faith.

This is the SAME payload the website and the MCP `get_market_indicators` tool render.
None of them re-words it, which is what stops the surfaces drifting apart.

Everything we compute about one stock, in plain English, with its contribution.

The per-ticker twin of `/market/indicators`, built from the same row type and the
same colour rule: the eight weighted components that make the conviction score,
the forecast band, the risk and sizing numbers, and every one of the risk checks
that can veto a BUY — each with a plain-English label, its current reading, what
that reading means, and which way it is pushing the verdict.

`aggregate.arithmetic` shows the sum that produces the score (a neutral stock
starts at 5.0 out of 10 and the scoring rows move it from there), so the verdict
can be checked rather than taken on faith. Risk checks carry no points — they are
vetoes — and the note says so.

Rows arrive pre-worded: this API, the MCP tool, the website and the crawler
edition all render the SAME sentences, which is what stops them drifting apart.

"Am I too late to buy this?" — answered as an instruction with a price in it.

The single most-repeated question a retail investor asks, and the one nobody
answers straight. The reply is a headline verdict, one instruction naming the
price you should and should not pay, and the level at which our own call is
wrong — a stop if there is a live plan, the top of our 90% forecast band if we
are telling you not to buy. It will say "yes, you're late" when our own
three-month estimate sits below today's price, because a missed trade is cheap
and a bad one is not.

The risk-gate trace comes back in `why`, below the answer: it is the receipt
for the verdict, not something the customer should have to interpret to get one.
Fear & Greed index (latest cached value).

Earnings calendar for one ticker: the next and last reporting dates, and how many days away the next one is.

A risk gate, not a convenience: swing BUYs are suppressed within 5 days
of earnings. Absence of data returns ``available: false`` with
HTTP 200 (a normal cold-cache state), never a 404. ``as_of`` anchors
data freshness so callers can reason about staleness.

Full quantum forecast across horizons.

Every horizon the model emits (1mo/3mo/6mo/1y) is available to every tier,
including free — the forecast itself is never gated, and never a
lever a paid plan buys. What paid tiers buy instead is depth, capacity,
automation and the personalised position layer.

Pass ``format=markdown`` (or ``Accept: text/markdown``) for the compact
markdown forecast card — same data.

The JSON envelope carries a top-level ``disclaimer`` sentence, the same one
the signals endpoints and the markdown card's footer carry.

Cross-ticker entanglement matrix: which S&P 500 names the quantum model expects to move together.

``entanglement`` is the Pearson correlation of the model's *forecast* return
paths (``mode=forecast``, default) — a forward-looking, model-implied
co-movement signal, **NOT** a claim about realised market correlation. Use it
as a diversification-risk lens (don't stack names that are one trade) and a
pairs/divergence lens. ``mode=realized`` gives the trailing-returns consensus
baseline for comparison. Every number is computed from real persisted scan
data; tickers with no usable series are reported in ``missing``, never imputed.

``basis=ensemble`` (forecast mode only) correlates across the model's
full forecast band envelope (q05/q25/mean/q75/q95) and averages the per-band
correlations, surfacing tail co-movement that the default ``basis=mean``
(mean curve only) understates. The method label switches to
``quantum_forecast_ensemble`` so the two are never conflated.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

parameters.name: mode

schema.description: forecast = Pearson correlation of the quantum model's forecast price curves (model-implied co-movement; the default, non-consensus signal). realized = correlation of trailing daily returns (consensus baseline).
schema.title: Mode

parameters.description: forecast = Pearson correlation of the quantum model's forecast price curves (model-implied co-movement; the default, non-consensus signal). realized = correlation of trailing daily returns (consensus baseline).

parameters.name: basis

schema.description: Forecast-mode correlation basis. mean (default) correlates the single mean forecast curve. ensemble correlates across the q05/q25/mean/q75/q95 band envelope and averages the per-band correlations, surfacing tail co-movement the mean curve misses. Ignored in realized mode.
schema.title: Basis

parameters.description: Forecast-mode correlation basis. mean (default) correlates the single mean forecast curve. ensemble correlates across the q05/q25/mean/q75/q95 band envelope and averages the per-band correlations, surfacing tail co-movement the mean curve misses. Ignored in realized mode.

schema.description: Universe size: top-N tickers by 3mo forecast growth (2–100).
schema.title: Top N

parameters.description: Universe size: top-N tickers by 3mo forecast growth (2–100).

get.description:
S&P 500 screener: which top-100 tickers have notable insider activity now.

"Notable" = a cluster buy (3+ distinct insiders buying within 10 days) or a
single buy that is >=2x that insider's own historical median buy size, in
the last 30 days. Empty `results` is a valid, honest answer — most weeks
have no qualifying activity. Cached ~12h; a periodic
``tasks.insider_pulse.refresh_insider_screener`` Procrastinate task keeps
that cache warm — this endpoint is cache-read-only and NEVER
triggers a live ~100-CIK EDGAR fan-out on a cold miss.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

Note: registered ABOVE `/insider/{ticker}` — FastAPI matches path
operations in registration order, and "screener" would otherwise be
captured as a literal ticker symbol by the dynamic route below.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

Paginated, dated feed of persisted SEC Form 4 insider transactions
across the full S&P 500.

Unlike `/insider/screener` (a rolling TOP-100 "notable this month"
snapshot with no history), this reads the durable ``insider_events``
Postgres store so callers can page back through real dated
history. Ordering is pure newest-filed-first — cluster-buy and
unusually-large flags are informational only and do not affect sort.

Query params:
- `page` (default 1), `per_page` (default 25, max 100).
- `window`: lookback in days from today (default 90, max 400 — the
  store's retention horizon).
- `type`: optional `"buy"` or `"sell"` filter on the SEC transaction
  code; omitted/other values return both.
- `ticker`: optional single-symbol filter, applied server-side over the
  whole stored history (so `total` and the page count stay correct under
  the filter, rather than the caller having to page through everything and
  filter client-side).

An empty `items` list with `total: 0` is a valid, honest answer (e.g.
before the first ingestion run, or a quiet window) — never an error.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell
recommendation, and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

Note: registered ABOVE `/insider/{ticker}` — FastAPI matches path
operations in registration order, and "feed" would otherwise be
captured as a literal ticker symbol by the dynamic route below.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

Site-wide feed: most recent 8-K filings across the S&P 500 (TOP-100) universe.

Each entry carries a grounded event type (derived from the filing's own
SEC Item number(s) — never LLM-guessed), a one-line AI summary grounded
in the actual filing text, and a link to the source accession. Empty
`filings` is a valid, honest answer for a quiet news day. Cached ~2h; a
periodic ``tasks.filings_digest.refresh_8k_feed_digest`` Procrastinate
task keeps that cache warm — this endpoint is cache-read-only
and NEVER triggers a live ~100-CIK EDGAR fan-out on a cold miss.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

Note: registered ABOVE `/filings/digest/{ticker}` — FastAPI matches path
operations in registration order, and "digest" alone has no ticker
segment so this is unambiguous, but kept consistent with the
`/insider/screener` vs `/insider/{ticker}` ordering convention above.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

Site-wide feed: most recent 10-K annual reports across the S&P 500 (TOP-100) universe.

Companion to `/filings/digest` (surfaces top 10-Ks alongside the
8-K card). Unlike the 8-K feed, entries are metadata-only — ticker,
filed date, and a link to the source accession, no AI summary — since a
10-K is far too long to cheaply excerpt/ground a one-liner in. Empty
`filings` is a valid, honest answer. Cached ~6h; a periodic
``tasks.filings_digest.refresh_10k_feed_digest`` Procrastinate task keeps
that cache warm — this endpoint is cache-read-only and NEVER
triggers a live ~100-CIK EDGAR fan-out on a cold miss.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

Note: registered ABOVE `/filings/digest/{ticker}` for the same reason as
`/filings/digest` above — "10-k" would otherwise be captured as a
literal ticker symbol by the dynamic route below.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

8-K Event Digest — recent 8-K filings for one ticker, AI-summarized.

For each filing: event type derived from the filing's own SEC Item
number(s) (ground truth, e.g. Item 5.02 = exec departure/appointment,
Item 2.02 = earnings results, Item 2.01 = M&A completion — never
LLM-guessed), a one-line AI summary grounded in the actual filed
document text, and a link to the source accession via `accession_url`.

Cache-read on the request path: a cold miss (this ticker's
latest 8-K hasn't been summarized yet) returns an instant item-label
entry (`summary_source: "pending"`) instead of blocking on an EDGAR
doc fetch + LLM call — generation is deferred to a background
Procrastinate task so the next request serves the real grounded
summary. Same precompute/prewarm convention as
`/api/insights/{ticker}/sector`.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

One dated, page-through history covering every SEC filing form we store.

The companion `/filings/8-k/feed` below is the same store narrowed to 8-Ks;
this endpoint is the whole thing, so a caller can show annual reports and
material events side by side without stitching two feeds together.

Query params:
- `form`: optional SEC form filter — currently `8-K` (material events) or
  `10-K` (annual reports). Omitted returns every form. A form we do not
  store is a 400, never a silently-empty page: "we don't carry that form"
  and "that form had no filings" are different answers and the caller
  deserves to be able to tell them apart.
- `ticker`: optional single-symbol filter.
- `event_type`: optional narrowing to one broad 8-K category derived from
  the SEC's own item numbers (e.g. "earnings", "exec_change").
- `page` / `per_page`: pagination. The response always carries `total`, so
  the caller never has to fetch everything to learn how much there is.

Both filters are applied **server-side**, over the entire stored history —
not over the current page — so `total` and the page count remain truthful
while a filter is on.

An empty result is a valid, honest answer (a quiet news day, or a ticker we
have no filings for). This endpoint reads only our own store and never
calls SEC EDGAR, so it cannot be made slow — or get us rate-limited — by
traffic.

Read-only surfacing of official public-record data — this is information,
not a buy/sell recommendation, and does not feed the model's
conviction/signal logic.

A dated, page-through history of 8-K filings (the reports a company must file when something material happens).

Different from the `/filings/digest` endpoint above, which only ever shows
a rolling snapshot of the current feed and cannot be paged back through.
This one is backed by a durable, append-only history, so you can walk back
as far as it goes. Newest filing first. `event_type` optionally narrows the
results to one broad category derived from the SEC's own filing items (for
example "earnings" or "exec_change").

An empty result is a valid, honest answer — most often a quiet news day.
This endpoint never fails because the history store is unavailable; it
degrades to an empty page.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

What changed in the language of one company's latest SEC filing, versus the comparable filing a year (or a quarter) earlier.

Covers the two sections where companies describe what could go wrong and
how management reads the business: Risk Factors and Management's
Discussion & Analysis.

Cites a known academic finding (Cohen, Malloy & Nguyen 2020, "Lazy
Prices", Journal of Finance): YoY changes in 10-K Risk Factors/MD&A
language are historically return-predictive. The similarity score is a
real TF-IDF cosine similarity computed between the two actual filing
sections; `added_sentences`/`removed_sentences` are a real sentence-level
diff. Every entry links to BOTH source filings via `filings[].accession_url`.

An empty `sections` dict is a valid, honest answer when fewer than 2
filings of the requested form are on file, or a section couldn't be
reliably extracted from both filings (see module docstring in
`quantum_model/filing_language_diff.py` for known extraction-format
gaps) — never fabricated.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

Cache-read-only (precompute+cache convention): the expensive diff (two
multi-MB filing downloads + sentence-level TF-IDF diff + up to two LLM
calls) NEVER runs on this request path. On a cold cache key the response is
``status="pending"`` (with both source-filing links already populated) and
a background worker computes+caches the diff; a follow-up request serves it.

Args:
    form: "10-K" (year-over-year, default) or "10-Q" (quarter-over-quarter).

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

A dated, page-through feed of institutional 13F holdings — who owns what, and how much.

Each row is one institutional holder × one security × one reported
quarter: the filer, the security (with its ticker where we can map the
CUSIP to one we cover), share count, reported dollar value, the quarter it
covers, the date it was filed, and a link to the source 13F accession.
Newest filing first; within a day the larger dollar positions lead.

Unlike `/institutional/{ticker}` (a per-ticker quarter-over-quarter whale
summary), this reads the durable ``institutional_holdings`` Postgres store
so callers can page back through real dated history.

Coverage is deliberately narrow — roughly 50 large institutional filers
over the last few quarters, NOT all 13F filings. `ticker` optionally
narrows to one symbol (server-side, so the `total` stays truthful under the
filter); a ticker we don't cover, or a holding whose CUSIP never mapped to
a symbol, yields an honest empty page.

An empty `items` list with `total: 0` is a valid, honest answer (e.g.
before the first ingestion run) — never an error. This endpoint never hits
EDGAR; it is a Postgres read only, and degrades to an empty page when the
store is unavailable.

Note: registered ABOVE `/institutional/{ticker}` — FastAPI matches path
operations in registration order, and "feed" would otherwise be captured as
a literal ticker symbol by the dynamic route below.

Read-only surfacing of first-source public records — this is information,
not a buy/sell recommendation, and does not feed the model's
conviction/signal logic.

What the big institutional investors and activist shareholders are doing in one ticker.

``whale_summary``: QoQ (quarter-over-quarter) change in institutional
ownership across a curated ~50-filer 13F universe — new positions
opened, positions closed, and the largest increases/decreases by dollar
value between the two most recent 13F quarters on file. Pure computed
deltas, no LLM. Institutional filer names come from SEC's own
submissions data (ground truth), and every filer row links to its
source 13F accession via `accession_url`.

``activist_alerts``: recent Schedule 13D (activist/control intent) and
13G (passive >5% stake) filings. 13D entries include a one-line AI
summary grounded strictly in the filing's own Item 4 ("Purpose of
Transaction") text when confidently extractable (`summary_source:
"llm"`); otherwise a factual fallback sentence (`summary_source:
"item_label"`) — never invented intent. 13G entries get a structured,
non-AI note (`summary_source: "structured"`). Every alert links to its
source filing via `accession_url`.

An empty/near-empty result (empty `activist_alerts`, or a `whale_summary`
with a `narration` explaining why there's nothing to compute) is a
valid, honest answer — never fabricated.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

Cache-read-only: this endpoint NEVER triggers the 13F universe rebuild
(an EDGAR fan-out over every tracked whale filer) — the periodic
``tasks.institutional_activity.refresh_institutional_activity``
Procrastinate task owns generation. On a cold/lapsed cache the payload is
served stale-but-labelled (`stale`, `cache_age_hours`, `cache_status`) or
as an honest "no data cached yet" state, rather than blocking the request
on a rebuild.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

Insider Pulse — recent SEC Form 4 insider transactions for one ticker.

Surfaces already-ingested Form 4 filings (the same EDGAR data feeding the
market model's `form4` stage) with analytical context per transaction:
buyer role (officer/director/10% owner), transaction size vs that
insider's own historical buy pattern (`size_vs_own_median`,
`is_unusually_large`), and cluster-buy detection (`is_cluster` — 3+
distinct insiders buying within a 10-day window). Every transaction links
to its source SEC filing via `accession_url`.

Read-only surfacing — this is information, not a buy/sell recommendation,
and does not feed the model's conviction/signal logic.

Cache-read-only (precompute+cache convention): the fast persisted-store read
is served directly for covered tickers. For an uncovered long-tail ticker
(store miss) the expensive live per-symbol FMP fetch NEVER runs on this
request path — the response is ``status="pending"`` and a background worker
runs+caches the fetch; a follow-up request serves it cache-only.

*Disclaimer: informational only; not investment advice.*

CorrelationMatrixResponse.title: CorrelationMatrixResponse
CorrelationMatrixResponse.description:
Cross-ticker entanglement matrix (full or single-ticker shape).

``extra=allow`` so the full-matrix shape (matrix/top_pairs/missing) and the
single-ticker shape (correlations/most_entangled/most_divergent/note) share
one model — the route returns whichever the request selected.

time.title: Time
time.description: Session timing: "amc" (after close), "bmo" (before open), or null.

EarningsNext.title: EarningsNext
EarningsNext.description: Next-upcoming earnings event (estimates only — not yet reported).

days_until_next.title: Days Until Next
days_until_next.description: How many calendar days from the `as_of` date until the company next reports earnings. Null when we do not know the date.

as_of.title: As Of
as_of.description: Date the calendar was computed (data-freshness anchor).

EarningsResponse.title: EarningsResponse
EarningsResponse.description:
Per-ticker earnings calendar.

A first-class risk gate: swing BUYs are suppressed within 5 days of
earnings, so an agent must be able to see the earnings clock to
reason about overnight gap risk. ``available: false`` (with HTTP 200)
signals "no earnings data" — a normal cold-cache state, not an error.

timestamp.title: Timestamp
timestamp.description: When the index was last updated (ISO 8601).

FearGreedResponse.title: FearGreedResponse
FearGreedResponse.description:
Fear & Greed index snapshot.

``value`` / ``label`` / ``timestamp`` are the flat, documented contract.
The upstream payload nests the same data under ``current``
({score, rating, updated_at}), which left all three declared fields null on
the wire; the route lifts them so the declared shape is the shape actually
returned. ``current`` / ``history`` / ``sub_indicator_scores`` still ride
along via ``extra="allow"`` for the consumers that already read them.

band_coverage_pct.title: Band Coverage Pct
band_coverage_pct.description: ALWAYS NULL. This API publishes no coverage percentage for an individual ticker. One exception applies by measurement CLASS, not by naming an endpoint: any row anywhere we publish that names a ticker plus a forecast start date as a worst individual window (e.g. GET /api/calibration, GET /api/calibration/tsfm) is a cell of that universe measurement, not a reading for this ticker. The key is retained so a consumer sees an explicit null rather than a vanished field. It used to carry the 3mo horizon's scan-time backtest coverage; that figure was withdrawn because it is a single hold-out window (effective sample size one) and because its HIGH end is a defect (band too wide to be informative) that reads as a good grade. Rank on band_reliability; read horizons.*.band_width_read for the direction of miss. Never entitlement-gated.

calibration_score.title: Calibration Score
calibration_score.description: ALWAYS NULL. Deprecated alias of band_coverage_pct, retained at the same permanent null so existing consumers see an explicit empty value rather than a missing key. The name wrongly implied a higher-is-better accuracy score; it was never one. See band_coverage_pct for why no per-ticker coverage percentage is published, and rank on band_reliability.

band_reliability.title: Band Reliability
band_reliability.description: Reliability of the 3mo band in [0.1, 0.9] — higher is better, and the field to rank tickers on. It survives the withdrawal of the coverage percentage because it is two-sided: it peaks when a nominal 90% band actually covers ~90% and decays above as well as below, so an over-wide band cannot score high and the score cannot be misread as a hit rate. Derived from the same single-window backtest, so treat it as a coarse ordering, not a measurement. Null when this ticker's cohort has no backtest. Never entitlement-gated.

regime_conditioned.title: Regime Conditioned
regime_conditioned.description: True when a live market snapshot conditioned this forecast. The field name is kept unchanged for existing integrations. Never entitlement-gated.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.description: Compact disclaimer sentence for this detachable JSON envelope — a machine consumer reads P(up), the CI90 band and growth_pct without rendering any page, so the notice travels with the payload.

ForecastResponse.title: ForecastResponse
ForecastResponse.description: Full multi-horizon quantum forecast for one ticker.

HistoryEvent.title: HistoryEvent
HistoryEvent.description:
A single event in a ticker's signal history.

The event payload is open-ended; extra fields are forwarded as-is.

MarketIndicatorsResponse.title: MarketIndicatorsResponse
MarketIndicatorsResponse.description:
Every market indicator, already worded for a human.

Rows arrive presentation-ready (label, display, meaning, colour, tooltip) so
that no consumer — this API, the MCP tool, the website or the crawler edition —
has to invent its own wording and drift away from the others.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: AUTHORITATIVE verdict tier — the same one the dashboard shows. One of Strong Buy / Buy / Neutral / Caution / Strong Avoid (there is no Bull/Bear vocabulary). This is the confidence-adjusted tier; `model_verdict` carries the tier before the low-confidence downgrade and differs only when `confidence_downgraded` is true.

model_verdict.title: Model Verdict
model_verdict.description: Verdict tier before the low-confidence downgrade. Diagnostic, not the answer.

confidence_downgraded.title: Confidence Downgraded
confidence_downgraded.description: True when confidence < 0.50 softened `verdict` one tier toward Neutral.

score.title: Score
score.description: Buying-conditions score, 0-100. HIGHER IS BETTER FOR BUYING. It is relative, not absolute: a z-score of the composite against its own trailing ~6 months of daily readings, so a low score means 'among the weakest readings in about six months', never a claim about what percentage of the market is 'healthy'. See `score_basis`.

buying_conditions.title: Buying Conditions
buying_conditions.description: Self-describing block: score, direction, plain-English label, colour, and what the score is measured against.

score_basis.title: Score Basis
score_basis.description: What the 0-100 score is measured against, in plain English (relative to its own trailing window).

overheating.title: Overheating
overheating.description: The froth check. READ `legs`, `state` and `headline`. `legs` is the two readings froth is actually made of, 0-100 each: how cheaply risk is priced (calm volatility, tight credit spreads) and how much the crowd is piling in (greed, stretched breadth). Froth means BOTH are high at once. `state` names the pair in plain English; `headline` is a one-line human summary (state + both leg scores). The composite AND-gate scalar is NOT a top-level field — it is degenerate as a headline (collapses to ~0 whenever either leg is ~0, reading identically for a calm, cheaply-priced market and for an outright panic), so it is demoted to `composite_gated.value`, labeled as meaningless without both legs. Computed ONLY from froth inputs, never derived from `score` above; includes a full component decomposition. Not a forecast.

computed_at.title: Computed At
computed_at.description: ISO-8601 UTC timestamp of when this snapshot was computed — the as-of stamp. Always present on a stored snapshot; use it to judge freshness before acting on the reading.

stale.title: Stale
stale.description: True when this snapshot is older than the most recent scheduled refresh that should already have run (the batch scan, 02:00 UTC Mon-Fri), or when it carries no usable timestamp. Weekends do not make a Friday reading stale — no refresh is scheduled while the market is shut. Stale data is still served with HTTP 200: reads never recompute, so the flag is the honest signal, not an error.

stale_reason.title: Stale Reason
stale_reason.description: Why the reading is stale: `missed_scheduled_refresh`, `no_timestamp`, or `unparseable_timestamp`. Null when fresh.

age_hours.title: Age Hours
age_hours.description: How many hours ago this snapshot was computed. Null when the snapshot carries no usable timestamp — never back-filled from now.

action_plan.title: Action Plan
action_plan.description: Market-level entry / sizing / exit plan. In exit, take-profit levels (tp1_price, tp2_price, reference_price) are null when no live SPY quote is available — signalled by price_levels_available: false. They are never zero-filled.

MarketResponse.title: MarketResponse
MarketResponse.description:
The market's current state — TWO independent readings, one direction each.

``score`` / ``buying_conditions`` answer "how favorable are buying conditions?"
(HIGH = more favorable). ``overheating`` answers "is this market frothy?" (HIGH =
hot). The second is NOT the first inverted: it is computed from froth
inputs only and can legitimately read "not hot" while buying conditions
are bad — which is how a weak market under a calm surface is described,
as opposed to a bubble.

The snapshot has a fixed core but grows extra keys over time;
``extra="allow"`` forwards them all without schema churn.

rr_ratio.title: Rr Ratio
rr_ratio.description: The measured conservative reward-to-risk (reward to the TP1 rung over risk to the stop), at 2-decimal storage precision. This is the value the >=2:1 sizing gate reads — NOT the swing planned R:R on `signal.rr_ratio`.

min_required.title: Min Required
min_required.description: The risk-first minimum this ratio is judged against (2.0).

meets_minimum.title: Meets Minimum
meets_minimum.description: Whether the measured ratio is at or above the 2:1 minimum. Descriptive only — a published BUY has already cleared it; a WAIT may carry a value below it as the reason the trade was stood aside.

basis.title: Basis
basis.description: Plain-English rendering of the ratio with the forecast price it was measured from, e.g. `1.8:1 (the forecast distribution's TP1 rung over risk to the stop, priced at the forecast's $100.00 — a per-trade measurement, not the ladder's planned target)`.

MeasuredRewardToRiskResponse.title: MeasuredRewardToRiskResponse
MeasuredRewardToRiskResponse.description:
Forecast-derived, per-trade reward-to-risk — the ratio the sizing gate binds on.

Distinct from ``signal.rr_ratio``, which is the swing ladder's PLANNED TP2
rung (a design constant that equals its configured multiple on every
publishable signal). This one is the conservative TP1 rung over risk to the
stop, both quantiles of the forecast's simulated path extrema — it varies
per ticker and routinely falls below the 2:1 floor, so it is a genuine
measurement of this setup rather than a fixed target. ``basis`` names the
forecast price it was measured from, so the two figures can never be
confused with each other or with the same levels re-priced at today's spot.

band_coverage_pct.title: Band Coverage Pct
band_coverage_pct.description: ALWAYS NULL. This API publishes no coverage percentage for an individual ticker, at any horizon. One exception applies by measurement CLASS, not by naming an endpoint: any row anywhere we publish that names a ticker plus a forecast start date as a worst individual window (e.g. GET /api/calibration, GET /api/calibration/tsfm) is a cell of that universe measurement, not a reading for this ticker. The key is retained so a consumer sees an explicit null rather than a vanished field. It used to carry the live scan's own backtest coverage; that figure was withdrawn because it is a single hold-out window (effective sample size one, so it swings on nothing but the start date), and because a bare coverage percent inverts on the reader — its HIGH end is a defect (band too wide to be informative) that reads as a good grade. Read band_width_read for the direction of miss, band_reliability to rank, and GET /api/calibration for the measured universe record.

backtest_ci90.title: Backtest Ci90
backtest_ci90.description: ALWAYS NULL. Deprecated alias of band_coverage_pct, retained at the same permanent null so existing consumers see an explicit empty value rather than a missing key. See band_coverage_pct for why no per-ticker coverage percentage is published.

band_reliability.title: Band Reliability
band_reliability.description: Reliability of this horizon's band in [0.1, 0.9] — higher is better, and the field to rank on. It survives the withdrawal of the coverage percentage because it is two-sided: it peaks when a nominal 90% band actually covers ~90% and falls away above as well as below, so an over-wide band cannot score high and the score cannot be misread as a hit rate. Derived from the same single-window backtest, so treat it as a coarse ordering, not a measurement. Null when this ticker's cohort has no backtest.

band_width_read.title: Band Width Read
band_width_read.description: Which way this ticker's 90% band missed on ONE backtested hold-out window, as a word — never a percentage. One of `ran-narrow` (band too tight; the real downside was wider than it looked), `about-right`, or `ran-wide` (band too wide to be informative — a DEFECT, not a good grade). Read it as a direction of miss only: it comes from a single window on a model computed without the coupling and haircut the served forecast applies. Absent when this ticker's cohort has no backtest. Always accompanied by band_width_note.

band_width_note.title: Band Width Note
band_width_note.description: The sentence that must travel with band_width_read: what the read was computed from, why its underlying percentage is not publishable, and where the measured universe record lives. Present exactly when band_width_read is.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.description: Scope of the published band-calibration record, for this horizon. It carries NO coverage figure for this ticker: `ci90_empirical_coverage` is always null, because coverage is measured across a twenty-name universe at a given forecast start date and no cell of the record is a property of one symbol. Keys: cohort (core | high_interest), scope, calibration_status (varies-by-start-date | not-published | not-backtested — a statement about what we publish, never a grade for this ticker), universe_ci90_range_pct (the lowest and highest coverage observed ACROSS start dates for the universe, whole percents, core cohort only), published_record, and a note. Read GET /api/calibration for the per-start-date table itself. Absent for horizons the record does not measure (e.g. 1mo).

QuantumHorizonResponse.title: QuantumHorizonResponse
QuantumHorizonResponse.description: Quantum model statistics for a single forecast horizon.

next_cursor.title: Next Cursor
next_cursor.description: Opaque cursor for the next page. Null when no more results or when limit was not specified. Pass as cursor= on the next request.

disclaimer.title: Disclaimer
disclaimer.description: Compact disclaimer sentence for this detachable JSON envelope — per-item citation is skipped on list surfaces, so this top-level field carries it instead.

verdict.title: Verdict
verdict.description: THE VERDICT — what the model thinks of this stock: BUY | WAIT | EXIT. This is the same field, with the same meaning, that the website shows in its verdict hero (labelled BULLISH / NEUTRAL / BEARISH via `verdict_label`), so an answer quoted from this API cannot contradict the page. Never null. NOTE: this field previously carried the ENTRY (timing) facet — that value now has its own name, `timing`, and is unchanged there.

verdict_label.title: Verdict Label
verdict_label.description: The verdict as a customer reads it: BULLISH | NEUTRAL | BEARISH. Descriptive rather than an instruction. EXIT/BEARISH means 'consider closing an existing long' — NEVER a short-sell call.

timing.title: Timing
timing.description: THE TIMING — whether to put money in RIGHT NOW: BUY | WAIT | AVOID | WATCH. A separate question from the verdict: a stock the model likes (verdict BUY) can still be a bad entry today (timing AVOID). This is the value the `verdict` field carried before the two facets were given separate names. Null when this row has no entry answer at all (no value and no suppression gate) — the whole facet is then null and no filter matches it.

timing_label.title: Timing Label
timing_label.description: The timing facet in plain English, e.g. 'No setup yet' — a reading of a setup that WAS evaluated. Null when a suppression gate withheld the entry facet before it could be evaluated; `timing_statement` carries the answer in that case, while `timing` keeps its stand-aside wire value for filtering. Also null — alongside every other entry field — when there is no entry answer at all.

timing_statement.title: Timing Statement
timing_statement.description: Set ONLY when a suppression gate withheld the entry facet rather than the swing engine evaluating it and standing aside: the non-directional statement a reader may see ('No entry signal today'). Never a substitute direction — null whenever a real entry value exists.

timing_reason.title: Timing Reason
timing_reason.description: The suppression gate's own words for why no entry was published, quoted from the scan's gate trace. Null when nothing was withheld.

timing_gate.title: Timing Gate
timing_gate.description: Id of the gate that withheld the entry facet, e.g. `regime`.

actionable.title: Actionable
actionable.description: True when there is a capital action to take: an entry to put on (a published BUY with a full trade plan), or an existing long to close (an EXIT verdict). False for every stand-aside.

entry_actionable.title: Entry Actionable
entry_actionable.description: True only for a published BUY carrying a full trade plan (entry, stop, take-profit ladder) — i.e. `actionable` restricted to new entries, excluding EXIT.

reason.title: Reason
reason.description: Plain-English reason for this verdict — why we do (or do not) publish a trade. NULLABLE: null when there is no entry answer at all (no entry value and no suppression gate). A sentence there would explain a decision that was never made.

gates_failed.title: Gates Failed
gates_failed.description: Ids of the suppression gates that fired for this ticker (e.g. `regime` — market conditions, `confluence`, `drawdown`, `correlation`) — empty for a published BUY.

SwingSignalResponse.title: SwingSignalResponse
SwingSignalResponse.description:
Swing trade signal derived from the 3-month quantum horizon.

Always populated — `null` is never an answer. When no trade is published
(suppressed by the market-conditions gate, the confluence gates, or the
risk/Kelly sizing gate) the verdict is an explicit non-actionable
WAIT/AVOID carrying the reason and the gates that fired.

The ONE exception is a missing answer rather than a negative one: when this
row carries no entry value AND no suppression gate fired, the whole ENTRY
facet is null — `timing`, `timing_label`, `timing_statement`,
`timing_reason`, `timing_gate`, `reason` and `invalidation_note` are all
`null`, and `entry_actionable` is false. Nothing was evaluated, so there is
nothing to state; a `WAIT` here would assert a stand-aside we never
computed. Such a row deliberately does NOT match `?timing=wait`. The
DIRECTION facet (`verdict` / `verdict_label`) still publishes normally.

TickerIndicatorsResponse.title: TickerIndicatorsResponse
TickerIndicatorsResponse.description:
The same sheet shape, for one stock rather than the whole market.

Deliberately the same envelope: one registry per subject, one row type, one
renderer. A separate schema here would be the first step back towards two
surfaces describing the same number in two different ways.

band_coverage_pct.title: Band Coverage Pct
band_coverage_pct.description: ALWAYS NULL. This API publishes no coverage percentage for an individual ticker. One exception applies by measurement CLASS, not by naming an endpoint: any row anywhere we publish that names a ticker plus a forecast start date as a worst individual window (e.g. GET /api/calibration, GET /api/calibration/tsfm) is a cell of that universe measurement, not a reading for this ticker. The key is retained so a consumer sees an explicit null rather than a vanished field. It used to carry the 3mo horizon's scan-time backtest coverage; that figure was withdrawn because it is a single hold-out window (effective sample size one) and because its HIGH end is a defect (band too wide to be informative) that reads as a good grade. Rank on band_reliability; read horizons.*.band_width_read for the direction of miss. Never entitlement-gated.

calibration_score.title: Calibration Score
calibration_score.description: ALWAYS NULL. Deprecated alias of band_coverage_pct, retained at the same permanent null so existing consumers see an explicit empty value rather than a missing key. The name wrongly implied a higher-is-better accuracy score; it was never one. See band_coverage_pct for why no per-ticker coverage percentage is published, and rank on band_reliability.

band_reliability.title: Band Reliability
band_reliability.description: Reliability of the 3mo band in [0.1, 0.9] — higher is better, and the field to rank tickers on. It survives the withdrawal of the coverage percentage because it is two-sided: it peaks when a nominal 90% band actually covers ~90% and decays above as well as below, so an over-wide band cannot score high and the score cannot be misread as a hit rate. Derived from the same single-window backtest, so treat it as a coarse ordering, not a measurement. Null when this ticker's cohort has no backtest. Never entitlement-gated.

regime_conditioned.title: Regime Conditioned
regime_conditioned.description: True when a live market snapshot was available at scan time and the signal was gated/adjusted by current market conditions. False when the scanner used the conservative fail-open default (Neutral). The field name is kept unchanged for existing integrations.

signal.description: The verdict for this ticker. Always present and populated — a ticker with no publishable trade returns an explicit non-actionable WAIT with its reason, never null.

reward_to_risk.description: Forecast-derived measured reward-to-risk (the ratio the sizing gate binds on), labelled distinctly from the swing planned R:R on `signal.rr_ratio`. Absent when the forecast produced no ladder.

TickerSignalResponse.title: TickerSignalResponse
TickerSignalResponse.description: Signal + quantum snapshot for one ticker.

TooLateResponse.title: TooLateResponse
TooLateResponse.description:
The answer to "am I too late to buy this?" — a sentence with a price in it.

Every field arrives pre-worded from the model row: the headline verdict, the
instruction the customer is meant to act on, the level at which our own call is
wrong, and (when the stock has run past our buy limit) what chasing it actually
costs. `levels` are the prices, each already coloured for the customer and
carrying its own tooltip; `why` is the risk-gate trace, which belongs *below*
the answer — it is the receipt, not the reading task.

WebhookQueuedResponse.title: WebhookQueuedResponse
WebhookQueuedResponse.description: Result of a TradingView webhook POST.
